data.gender_notes: Aamirat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who commands, rules, and leads the army. The name Aamirat carries the meaning “Prince, Ruler, Commander” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Aamirat usually hope their child will grow to embody prince, ruler, commander and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner strength and courage to overcome challenges and lead others to success
data.etymology: Aamirat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Prince, Ruler, Commander.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aamirat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Aamirat
in_english.long_meaning: Aamirat is an Arabic name derived from the root Amr, meaning strength and courage, and it refers to a woman who is strong and a good companion, this name has a positive meaning in Islamic tradition and carries a deep spiritual significance related to leadership and care

data.cultural_impact: The name "Aamir" is associated with courage, leadership, and authority in Islamic culture. It is a name that evokes images of commanding military leaders and valiant warriors. Historically, it has been given to strong and capable individuals, reflecting the Arabic origins of the name. In modern times, it is a popular choice for boys in the Muslim world, continuing to symbolize power and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Aamir" serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate authority and leadership in our lives. It encourages us to strive for leadership roles and use our God-given abilities to command righteousness and guide others towards the Path of Allah. Additionally, the name "Aamir" can be interpreted as "the commander of the faithful," emphasizing the importance of faith and obedience to Allah in fulfilling our roles as leaders and followers.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aamir means the one who is in control or the leader. In a spiritual sense, it symbolizes one who guides others towards the right path, representing courage, leadership and responsibility.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Aamir bin Al-Aas was the second Umayyad caliph, ruling from 656 to 661 AD. He is known for expanding the Umayyad Caliphate's territories in the Mediterranean and Middle East, including conquering Egypt and Syria. The name 'Aamir' is believed to have derived from the Arabic root meaning 'commander' or 'leader'.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate, Expansion in Mediterranean and Middle East

historical_references.reference: Aamir ibn Sa'd was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He participated in various battles and was appointed as the governor of Kufa by Umar ibn Al-Khattab. The name 'Aamir' in this context is believed to have been a title given to him due to his leadership skills and military prowess.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, Military commander and governor under Umar ibn Al-Khattab
